coverage.stoppingReason: Bounded assignment stopped after primary-source reconstruction of four evidence-rich families and eligibility triage of every named seed; long-tail fork discovery remains incomplete.

eligibility.reason: Live before and during the scope window; canonical proportional elastic-supply monetary protocol.

lineage.relationship: fixed-balance wrapper representing a fixed share of AMPL market capitalization

versions.label: Ethereum elastic-supply system
versions.tokenRoles: AMPL is the rebasing unit; internal gons remain fixed while fragments shown by balanceOf vary. WAMPL later wraps a constant network share into a fixed token balance.
versions.backing: No collateral pool or contractual par redemption.
versions.redemption: No protocol redemption at the target; price convergence relies on market trading and supply response.
versions.supplyPolicy: Authorized monetary policy changes total fragments proportionally; holders retain the same supply percentage absent transfers. Positive nominal balance changes do not themselves create wealth because price and market capitalization remain market outcomes.
versions.debtAndIncentives: No protocol debt leg. Arbitrage/speculation must absorb inventory risk and delayed feedback.
versions.oracle: Market-price and CPI oracles feed policy; exact historical source mix/window varied and was not reconstructed commit-by-commit here.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Token owner can set the monetary-policy address in the retrieved current code; historical ownership transitions require transaction-level reconstruction.
versions.liquidityDependencies: DEXs and integrations must tolerate balance changes; fixed-balance wrappers reduce integration friction but add wrapper dependency.

eligibility.reason: Launched in August 2020 as an elastic-supply token targeting 1 USDC; versions and later cessation are directly documented.

lineage.relationship: YAM adopted proportional elastic-supply accounting and added treasury seigniorage

versions.label: YAMv1
versions.tokenRoles: Rebasing YAM also carried governance votes; internal underlying balances were distinct from scaled visible balances.
versions.backing: Unbacked as to par; positive-rebase seigniorage attempted to acquire reserve assets.
versions.supplyPolicy: Targeted 1 USDC with proportional rebases; intended reserve mint-and-sale path contained a scaling error.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Farming distributed tokens; rebase expansion funded a governance treasury rather than a holder redemption claim.
versions.oracle: Contemporary v1 materials identify an on-chain pool price, but this report does not assert a fully reconstructed window for the failed version.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Rebase overmint inflated supply/votes enough to make quorum unattainable and freeze governance-controlled reserves.
versions.liquidityDependencies: YAM/yCRV Uniswap V2 residual LPs faced continuing excess-mint/sale risk.

versions.label: YAMv2 migration placeholder
versions.tokenRoles: Standard non-rebasing ERC-20 placeholder for migration and signaling.
versions.redemption: v1 could be burned for v2 during a short migration window, based on balanceOfUnderlying; this was migration, not par redemption.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Temporary bridge to an audited relaunch.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Migration deadline created operational risk for inactive holders.

versions.label: YAMv3 audited relaunch and post-rebase governance token
versions.tokenRoles: Initially restored rebasing YAM; after policy disablement, governance token with scaling factor fixed at 2.50.
versions.backing: Governance treasury is not a contractual redemption reserve.
versions.supplyPolicy: Used SushiSwap YAM/ETH TWAP; no rebase inside 0.95–1.05 USDC; 5% of positive rebase amount was minted/sold for treasury ETH. Governance disabled rebasing on 2020-12-29.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Treasury capture shifted some expansion away from pro-rata holders and imposed sell pressure on LPs.
versions.oracle: YAM/ETH SushiSwap TWAP according to archived official docs.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Community governance could and did disable rebasing.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Treasury sale executed through SushiSwap and therefore depended on pool depth and execution.

incidents.summary: A scaling error caused reserve overmint; no attacker was required. Vote inflation broke quorum and locked treasury governance.
incidents.beneficiaries: No demonstrated attacker; some liquidity providers exited before later rebases.
incidents.lossBearers: Residual YAM/yCRV LPs and holders exposed to the failed system and migration friction.
incidents.outcome: Rescue failed; v2 migration followed, then audited v3. This was a code/governance coupling failure, not evidence that price feedback alone caused the failure.

incidents.summary: Governance disabled elastic supply because it added friction unnecessary for the governance-token role.
incidents.beneficiaries: Integrators and holders seeking fixed balances.
incidents.outcome: YAM continued as a non-rebasing governance token.

protocols.name: Base Protocol

eligibility.reason: Code and contemporaneous paper evidence show a 2020 elastic-supply implementation targeting a crypto-market-cap index.

protocols.targetUnit: One trillionth of total cryptocurrency market capitalization (project-stated)

lineage.relationship: Code-derived proportional hidden-share accounting; independent target and added blacklist logic

versions.label: BASE elastic index token
versions.tokenRoles: BASE balances derive from hidden shares.
versions.backing: No portfolio of indexed assets evidenced.
versions.supplyPolicy: Monetary-policy contract changes total supply proportionally.
versions.oracle: Target necessarily depended on external aggregate crypto-market-cap data; exact production oracle path unresolved.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Retrieved token code permits owner to change monetary policy and maintain a user ban list.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Market arbitrage rather than basket creation/redemption.

eligibility.reason: Verified explorer source identifies deployed elastic-supply DEBASE and governance-configured stabilizer pools.

versions.label: DEBASE production token
versions.backing: Stabilizer pools are incentive/liquidity mechanisms, not demonstrated unconditional redemption backing.
versions.supplyPolicy: Elastic supply controlled by debasePolicy with allocations to configured pools.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Pool rewards intended to influence liquidity and price response.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Depends on stabilizer-pool participation and market liquidity.

eligibility.reason: BadgerDAO launched a BTC-targeting elastic-supply asset in January 2021 and later documented peg failure and cessation.

lineage.relationship: Code-level uFragments-style gon accounting with a BTC rather than CPI-dollar target
vault receipt token, not 1:1 DIGG and not itself the monetary base

versions.label: Daily BTC-target rebase
versions.tokenRoles: DIGG rebases; bDIGG is an interest-bearing Sett vault receipt; BADGER governance and Boost supplied auxiliary demand.
versions.backing: Official product page explicitly says DIGG was not backed by Bitcoin under management.
versions.supplyPolicy: Daily: expand above 1.05 BTC, contract below 0.95 BTC, unchanged inside band; proportional holder share remains unchanged.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Vault emissions and Badger Boost rewarded holding/liquidity, creating demand not equivalent to redeemability.
versions.oracle: BTC and DIGG market-rate oracle contracts existed; precise historical window/feeder set not fully reconstructed.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: BadgerDAO governed policy and later restructuring.
versions.liquidityDependencies: SushiSwap DIGG/WBTC and vaults were key integration points; rebasing pool balances require sync-aware handling.

incidents.summary: Badger governance recorded that prior rebase changes had not maintained the 1:1 BTC target and DIGG traded around a 50% discount.
incidents.beneficiaries: Not established; emissions recipients received tokens but value transfer is not quantified.
incidents.lossBearers: DIGG holders and liquidity providers bore price decline and inventory/impermanent-loss exposure; BADGER holders faced proposed dilution trade-offs.
incidents.outcome: Proposal moved DIGG to free float, stopped rebasing and external LP support, and ended DIGG emissions.

eligibility.reason: The seed name is heavily confounded with a later unrelated Ditto Network. No retrieved primary 2020–2021 contract or canonical repository was sufficient to verify mechanics or deployment.

protocols.name: RAI

eligibility.reason: Materially active in 2021 and intentionally relevant to monetary controllers, but official docs state it is not a rebase token.

protocols.targetUnit: Floating redemption price denominated in USD; no fixed peg

lineage.relationship: GEB collateralized-debt architecture with a floating controller target rather than fixed-dollar peg

versions.label: RAI mainnet managed float
versions.tokenRoles: RAI is debt generated from ETH-collateralized SAFEs; FLX supports governance/backstop functions. Holder token balances do not rebase.
versions.backing: ETH collateral in SAFEs, with liquidation and system accounting; collateral backing is distinct from the controller's moving redemption price.
versions.redemption: No routine fixed-dollar redemption. Redemption price governs debt/collateral accounting and collateral claims in Global Settlement.
versions.supplyPolicy: Supply expands when borrowers mint RAI and contracts when debt is repaid/liquidated; PID policy changes the redemption rate, which compounds the redemption price rather than wallet balances.
versions.debtAndIncentives: If market price is below redemption price, a positive redemption rate makes debt more expensive over time and rewards holders in settlement terms; above target, negative rate does the reverse. Borrow rate is separate.
versions.oracle: Secondary-market RAI price TWAP and ETH collateral oracle feed separate controller and solvency functions; production automation documentation shows 12-hour minimum TWAP update cadence and 30-minute pinger scheduling, but current docs cannot silently prove all 2021 settings.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Governance-minimization was stated; parameter and shutdown powers persisted in the system's staged architecture.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Controller action relies on SAFE users and holders trading/borrowing in response; thin liquidity, delayed response and bounded willingness to take ETH/debt risk constrain arbitrage.

eligibility.reason: Repository claims an AMPL fork and lists a token address, but policy/oracle addresses remain TBD and retrieved evidence does not establish materially active monetary operation in-window.

claims.statement: AMPL uses proportional elastic-supply accounting: rebase changes fragments per fixed gon, preserving each non-trading holder's supply share.
claims.uncertainty: Historical implementation changes not exhaustively diffed.

claims.statement: AMPL has no collateral redemption at its target; a rebase changes nominal units, not automatically holder wealth.
claims.evidenceLocator: token rebase implementation and protocol description
claims.reasoning: No redemption path appears in token policy; proportional ownership is unchanged, so wealth remains a function of market capitalization.
claims.uncertainty: Inference is architectural, not a measured return study.

claims.statement: The official contracts README lists the Ethereum token, policy, orchestrator, market oracle and CPI oracle addresses.
claims.uncertainty: Explorer verification was not independently checked.

claims.statement: WAMPL fixes visible token balances while each unit represents a fixed percentage ownership of AMPL market capitalization.
claims.reasoning: Direct code documentation and conversion design.

claims.statement: YAM launched in August 2020 targeting 1 USDC and combined proportional rebasing with treasury seigniorage.
claims.uncertainty: Docs say August 12 in one location and recap says August 11; farming launch used August 11, rebase phase followed.

claims.statement: The v1 rebase bug minted far more reserve YAM than intended and made governance quorum unreachable.
claims.uncertainty: No independent transaction-level loss quantification here.

claims.statement: Residual YAM/yCRV Uniswap V2 liquidity remained unsafe because later positive rebases would route excess minting through the pool.
YAMv2 was a non-rebasing migration placeholder minted by burning v1 based on balanceOfUnderlying, before audited v3.
claims.uncertainty: Exact deployment date/address not verified here.

claims.statement: YAMv3 used a SushiSwap YAM/ETH TWAP, a 0.95–1.05 USDC no-rebase band, and treasury capture equal to 5% of the positive rebase amount.
claims.uncertainty: Exact TWAP window omitted in retrieved page.

claims.statement: Governance disabled YAM rebasing on 2020-12-29 because it created unnecessary friction for a governance token.
BASE copied proportional hidden-denomination accounting but targeted a crypto-market-cap index and added owner-controlled monetary policy and user banning.
claims.evidenceLocator: BaseToken.sol header, setMonetaryPolicy, setUserBanStatus; paper target section
claims.reasoning: Code supports mechanics; mirrored paper supports stated target.

claims.statement: The verified DEBASE contract is an elastic token controlled by debasePolicy with configured DEBASE/DAI and LP stabilizer-pool allocations.
claims.evidenceLocator: Etherscan exact-match source and initialize ABI
claims.uncertainty: Controller/oracle and historical parameters not reconstructed.

claims.statement: DIGG was uncollateralized, targeted 1 BTC, and rebased daily outside a ±5% band while preserving holder supply percentage.
bDIGG was a vault receipt whose exchange rate to DIGG could rise; it was not a 1:1 wrapper.
DIGG token code uses UFragments-style fixed-gon accounting and restricts rebase to the monetary policy.
claims.uncertainty: Formal fork commit ancestry not established.

claims.statement: By April 2022 governance described DIGG near a 50% BTC discount and proposed free float, stopping rebases, emissions and external LP support.
claims.reasoning: DAO governance record supplies hindsight outcome.
claims.uncertainty: Execution and exact market observation were not independently verified.

claims.statement: Eligibility and mechanics of the 2020–2021 DITTO seed remain unresolved from retrieved primary evidence.
claims.reasoning: Searches were dominated by an unrelated later Ditto Network; similarity of names is not ancestry evidence.

claims.statement: RAI is an ETH-backed managed float, not a rebase token; wallet token quantities do not change.
claims.evidenceLocator: FAQ What is RAI? and Is RAI a rebase token?

claims.statement: RAI's redemption price normally floats and is used for SAFE accounting and Global Settlement, not as a promise of routine fixed-dollar redemption.
A PID controller changes the redemption rate in response to sustained market/redemption-price error, transferring incentives between SAFE debtors and holders.
claims.uncertainty: Actual parameter epochs changed over time.

claims.statement: RAI collateral solvency accounting, borrow rate, and redemption-rate monetary controller are separate mechanisms.
claims.evidenceLocator: FAQ redemption vs borrow rate and settlement sections

claims.statement: Production automation configuration documents 30-minute pinger scheduling and a 720-minute minimum TWAP update interval, but is not proof those were the settings throughout 2021.
claims.reasoning: Direct current repository configuration with temporal caveat.

claims.statement: reBΔSE's repository calls itself an Ampleforth fork but leaves supply-policy and oracle addresses TBD.
claims.reasoning: Repository claim is evidence of asserted lineage, not operational deployment.
